(2) THE ANSWER IS THE SERVER'S, PER CELL: zonefield.ts asks shared resolveAmbientAt per cell (never a second rule), blurs a cell each way and reads bilinearly — 0 outside, 1 inside, a ramp ~3 cells wide, half-on ON the line. (3) A ZONE RE-ROLLS SOMEWHERE EVERY ~6 s (96 zones phased over 10 min; measured 8 refreshes in 40 s): a memo that clears world-wide on every table change re-resolves the whole view for a change on the far side of the map — prune by the zone ids a cell's memo touched. (4) ISO PIXELS -> CELLS GOES THROUGH THE PICKER, memoised per 16x8 bucket: on a terraced edge one pixel of a straight line lands on the terrace it is DRAWN on, which is right for a particle at that pixel and wrong for a monotonicity test — assert the ramp in cell space (__mlAmbient.zoneCell), report the pixel walk. (5) HEADLESS CHROMIUM RUNS THIS PAGE AT 2-5 FPS (measured, 960x600 and 1280x720): a wait counted in frames is half a minute at 80 frames and blows any timeout — a gate waits in TIME. (6) A STAND POINT IS THE POLYGON'S EDGE AT A ROW, not its bounding box (a sea's box is far from its shore), on flat ground (world 'level'), where no OTHER zone carries the same effect over the stand cell (a neighbour's leaves read as this zone's). (7) pkill -f with the script's name in the pattern kills the shell that is about to run it — twice today.
